item.title: TBG Closed Sept 3, 2026 — Thu Sep 3, 12:00 AM
item.description:
The Toronto Botanical Garden Visitor Centre will be closed to the public on Thursday, September 3, 2026 following Toronto’s significant rain event.
The Garden experienced moderate flooding and water intrusion in several areas of the building. On the advice of our City of Toronto partners, we are closing for the day to allow our teams to assess the situation, complete necessary cleanup and determine next steps.
As a result the Visitor Centre, including the Garden Shop and Library will be closed. In addition, all programs, TBG Camp, volunteer activities and private events scheduled for September 3 are cancelled.
We appreciate your patience and understanding as we work to ensure the Garden is safe for our visitors, staff and volunteers.
We will share further updates as they become available.
Source: Toronto Botanical Garden

item.title: The Quote-to-Cash Blind Spot: Secret Scanning for Enterprise Revenue Systems — Wed Sep 9, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto Every CPQ, CLM, and billing rollout I've run wires Salesforce or Vlocity to DocuSign, Stripe or Zuora-type billing, and ERP through API keys and OAuth tokens sitting in DataRaptors, Integration Procedures, and deployment scripts. AppSec teams usually classify that layer as "business configuration," so it never gets scanned the way application code does.
Where credentials actually live in a quote-to-cash stack: middleware scripts, integration procedures, CI/CD for CPQ deployments. Why "business systems" teams don't think of themselves as a scanning target, and what that costs. How GitHub Advanced Security's secret scanning, push protection, and custom patterns close the gap, even for teams that don't see themselves as developers.
A sample repo modeling a CPQ integration script with a hardcoded OAuth token and API key. Push protection blocking a commit in real time. A custom regex pattern built for an enterprise revenue-tool token format. The alert triage view

item.description:
This is a ride to watch the salmon run on the Ganaraska River. People go to Port Hope every weekend from mid-August to early October to watch the 5,000 to 10,000 chinook and silvery coho salmon swim from Lake Ontario up the Ganaraska River that runs through Port Hope on their way to their home spawning grounds. The two cycling routes (below) are based on the Newcastle Navigator Country Cruise which leave from Newcastle and head north-east to Port Hope for lunch. Each route has four optional stops to watch the Salmon Run (see cue sheets for details) before getting to Port Hope. item.description: Join author Allison Rumfitt and filmmaker David Prior as they discuss Kiyoshi Kurosawa's techno-thriller masterpiece with host Adam Nayman. In this first instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series on Horror Classics on Film, writer and critic Alison Rumfitt, filmmaker David Prior, and host Adam Nayman discuss Pulse, Kiyoshi Kurosawa's sinister techno-thriller film. Imagining a world where the internet becomes a breeding ground for malevolent spirits, the film's artistry lies in the spine-tingling power of suggestion rather than a barrage of blood and guts. item.title: Author Talk with Dr. Kirsten Johnson on Humanitarienne: A Doctor’s Stories from the Conflict Zone — Wed Oct 7, 10:00 AM
item.description: As a physician and public health specialist, Dr. Kirsten Johnson has led missions in conflict zones, disaster-stricken regions and underserved communities. In her book, Humanitarienne: A Doctor's Stories from the Conflict Zone , she traces how a strict childhood marked by trauma pushed her to seek independence early. Join this 1-hour presentation where Johnson shares her story as a global health expert working in some of the world's most volatile places and how she pushed back on inequities embedded in humanitarian systems. If you're drawn to international work, social justice, or the ways in which people are shaped by—and in turn shape the world around them, this presentation will inspire you. Presented as part of Women's History Month. Registration: This virtual event is free to join and will take place on Zoom .
